newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOK WING WILLIAMS SET TO MISS SECOND YEAR.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOK WING WILLIAMS SET TO MISS SECOND YEAR.

text.p: Springbok wing Chester Williams faces another year out of rugby after breaking down with injury in only his second comeback match.

Williams -- the only non-white member of South Africa's World Cup-winning team of 1995 -- tore cruciate ligaments in his left knee playing for Western Province against Griqualand West on Thursday night.
The injury cruelly mirrors torn knee ligaments he suffered in his right knee 13 months ago which kept him out for the entire 1996 season.
"They say that lightning doesn't strike twice but it does," said Williams.

But he remained optimistic despite the latest setback: "Take it as a promise that when Western Province play their first match of next year Chester Williams will be on the left wing in the number 11 jersey."

The powerful, 26-year-old Williams made his Springbok debut against Argentina in 1993. The highlight of his World Cup -- apart from playing in the final -- was to score four tries against Western Samoa in South Africa's 42-14 quarter-final win.
He finished the 1995 season with a brace of tries against England at Twickenham and was expected to figure in new coach Carel du Plessis's plans for the visit of the British Lions in May and June.
